transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-29 15:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Product), Ethan Chen (Head of ML, NovaSearch), Rina Gupta (ML Engineer), Sam Ortega (Infra Lead)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete): Customer evaluating quant profiles for search rerank, wants low-latency tail, worried about quality degradation on INT8, considering FP8 and mixed precision. Redwood demoed Optimize UI, quantization presets, and quality/latency matrix.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Lena from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account, joining with Marcus the SE and Priya from product. How are you all?
[00:06] Ethan Chen: Good, thanks Lena. Excited to see the quantization stuff.
[00:09] Rina Gupta: Yep, we've got a heavy reranking workload so latency and P50/P99 matter a lot.
[00:14] Marcus Li: Great, we'll focus on the Optimize walkthrough — specifically the INT8 and FP8 quant profiles, show you the quality vs latency comparisons we typically see, and then talk about how batching and KV cache change the economics.
[00:24] Sam Ortega: Quick ask up front — we are likely to push Dedicated if latencies look good, but security + KMS integration is required.
[00:30] Lena Park: Noted, we'll also share the security appendix. Marcus, do you want to kick off with the profile overview?
[00:36] Marcus Li: Sure. So in Optimize you have a set of quantization profiles — we surface defaults like INT8-optim, FP8-balanced, plus model-specific profiles for things like Llama2-70B, Mistral, etc. The main tradeoff is precision vs model size / throughput. For our benchmarks on open models we often see INT8 drop quality by roughly 8-15% on worst-case gen metrics for large dense models, whereas FP8 tends to be in the 3-7% range but with more GPU memory usage.
[01:02] Rina Gupta: When you say 8-15% is that BLEU-like metrics or human eval? Our rerank is precision@10 and some human judgment.
[01:08] Marcus Li: It's mixed — mostly automated metrics we track (exact-match/rouge for some tasks) and some curated human evals. For rerank specifically the degradation is often smaller in practice — maybe 3-8% relative to FP16 baseline — but we need your prompt set to validate.
[01:20] Ethan Chen: Ok, that aligns with our expectation. What's the latency wins?
[01:23] Marcus Li: With INT8 you can see up to 2x throughput improvement and 25-40% reduction in p50/p99 latency depending on batch size and model. FP8 typically gives around 1.2-1.6x throughput and 10-25% latency reduction. These are rough numbers; sequence length and KV cache hit-rate matter a lot.
[01:40] Sam Ortega: KV cache hit-rate — can you quantify? We're doing a lot of short prefix queries then full expansion.
[01:45] Marcus Li: If you have high cache hits (>=70%), effective latency for repeated prefixes drops dramatically; batching helps too. In Explore we show how continuous batching and prefix caching combine to reduce per-token cost.
[02:00] Rina Gupta: Is there any additional model surgery or re-training for INT8? Our legal team doesn't want to change model weights.
[02:06] Marcus Li: No weight re-training — quantization is an offline conversion step. For some models we use symmetric vs asymmetric quant schemes; Optimize chooses profiles based on validation prompts. In a few edge cases we recommend a light calibration run but not re-training.
[02:20] Priya Rao: Also worth noting we provide per-prompt quality deltas so you can see which prompt types degrade most. That helps decide whether to use mixed precision or fallbacks for specific routes.
[02:33] Ethan Chen: Mixed precision sounds interesting — can I have certain routes use FP8 while others INT8?
[02:37] Lena Park: Absolutely — you can pin routes to profiles in Redwood Console and set automatic fallbacks. For example, critical paths can use FP8 or FP16 while bulk tasks use INT8.
[02:48] Sam Ortega: How does this affect cost? Any ballpark numbers?
[02:51] Marcus Li: In our customers we typically see unit token cost drop 30-60% on INT8 vs FP16 depending on GPU and utilization; FP8 sits in between. The dominant factor is throughput and whether you can increase batch sizes without hurting tail latency.
[03:08] Rina Gupta: Tail latency is our hard SLO — p99 under 350ms for rerank. Can INT8 hit that?
[03:13] Marcus Li: Possibly, especially on Dedicated with pinned capacity and tuned batching. On hosted endpoints you can also get there but you need to set concurrency and routing policies. We'll run your sample prompts to measure.
[03:25] Ethan Chen: Great, let's talk benchmarking flow.
[03:27] Marcus Li: We recommend: 1) provide 1k representative prompts; 2) we run bench across FP16, FP8, INT8 with your target sequence lengths; 3) we produce quality vs latency curves and per-prompt deltas; 4) we recommend profiles and fallback policies. That usually takes 3-7 days depending on queue.
[03:44] Rina Gupta: Who owns infra for the bench? Can we run it on our Dedicated trial?
[03:48] Lena Park: We can run benches on Redwood Dedicated trial or on your Private deployment if you prefer. For security-sensitive data you can run the conversion and bench in your VPC; we provide the scripts and config.
[03:58] Sam Ortega: KMS support? HSM?
[04:00] Priya Rao: We integrate with customer KMS providers and can support HSM-backed keys for private deployments. We'll share the security appendix with specifics.
[04:09] Ethan Chen: Ok. Any gotchas with FP8 — e.g., instability or numeric issues?
[04:13] Marcus Li: FP8 is newer; for certain attention patterns you can see occasional outlier tokens or hallucinations on edge cases. Optimize flags those cases in the per-prompt delta report; we also recommend mixing precision or using per-route fallbacks.
[04:29] Rina Gupta: Can you show the Optimize UI for the quant profiles?
[04:32] Marcus Li: Sure, sharing screen now. (screen share noise)
[04:36] Marcus Li: Here is the profile matrix — on the x-axis latency, y-axis quality delta; each dot is a profile tested on your validation set. You can click a dot to see per-prompt diffs and example generations.
[04:48] Lena Park: You'll notice the FP8-balanced dot sits near the top-left for many models — moderate latency improvement with small quality loss. INT8-optim sits further right with bigger latency gain but wider quality spread.
[05:00] Rina Gupta: I see some prompts with big deltas — looks like long-form summarization suffers more.
[05:04] Marcus Li: Exactly — longer generations amplify quant noise. For rerank, shorter context, INT8 is often fine.
[05:10] Ethan Chen: How much of this is model-dependent? We're evaluating Llama2-70B and a smaller in-house model.
[05:15] Marcus Li: Very model dependent. Llama2 variants tolerate INT8 differently than other architectures. We ship model-specific profiles and recommend running the bench on each model. For your in-house model we'll need a model artifact to create a profile.
[05:30] Sam Ortega: For private deployment, is the quant conversion process supported in-air gapped clusters?
[05:34] Marcus Li: Yes, we provide an offline conversion tool that can run in air-gapped environments; we send the binary and the scripts.
[05:40] Rina Gupta: What about reproducibility — will results be the same on different GPU types?
[05:45] Marcus Li: Kernel implementations can differ — e.g., A100 vs H100 may show slightly different perf. Optimize's runner records hardware metadata so you can compare apples-to-apples. We also recommend pinning CUDA and cuDNN versions.
[05:58] Ethan Chen: Any recommended sequence length trimming or chunking to help latency?
[06:02] Marcus Li: Yes, prefix caching and trimming repeated boilerplate helps a lot. You can also use early stopping heuristics. We'll show an example in the bench report.
[06:12] Lena Park: Quick interjection — price/SPU question from procurement: if we go Dedicated what does pricing look like for reserved capacity with INT8 optimizations?
[06:20] Priya Rao: Pricing depends on reserved vGPU type and utilization. Because INT8 increases effective throughput, you often need fewer GPUs for the same requests, reducing monthly committed spend. We'll include a cost model in the bench spreadsheet.
[06:34] Sam Ortega: Do you support autotune where Redwood picks profile based on observed quality drift?
[06:39] Marcus Li: We have quality monitoring and auto-rollout policies. If quality drifts beyond your threshold, we can automatically rollback to the previous profile or route to FP16. It's configurable per-route.
[06:50] Rina Gupta: That's great. Any regulatory concerns about quantization changing model outputs for audit?
[06:55] Marcus Li: We log per-inference metadata and store diffs for flagged prompts. Audit trails can show which profile served a given request. For Private deployments, logs stay in your environment.
[07:08] Ethan Chen: Ok last... can you summarize recommended next steps for a pilot?
[07:12] Marcus Li: 1) Customer share 1k prompts + evaluation criteria. 2) Redwood runs bench on FP16/FP8/INT8 for both Llama2-70B and your small model. 3) Deliver report with per-prompt deltas, latency curves, and recommended profiles. 4) Demo results and decide route pinning.
[07:31] Lena Park: Sounds good. Anything else?
[07:33] Ethan Chen: Please include security docs and KMS integration details.
[07:36] Lena Park: Will do.
[07:38] Priya Rao: Also attaching sample console screenshots and benchmark template after the call.
[07:43] Rina Gupta: Great, thanks.
[07:45] Sam Ortega: Thanks, appreciate the thoroughness.
[07:47] Lena Park: Ok we'll follow up with the artifacts and schedule the kickoff for the first week of April.

[45:08] Ethan Chen: Perfect.
